M10_S01.summary: The study of the cognitive series rests on six sets of six — bases, doors, objects, consciousnesses, processes and modes of presentation of the object.
body: For the compendium of the cognitive process one must know six groups of six: the 6 bases (vatthu), the 6 doors (dvāra), the 6 objects (ālambana), the 6 consciousnesses (viññāṇa), the 6 processes (vīthi) and the 6 modes in which an object presents itself (visayappavatti).
The six consciousnesses are: eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness and mind-consciousness.
Classified by door, the cognitive processes are six: the processes through the eye-door, ear-door, nose-door, tongue-door, body-door and mind-door.
For the cittas that fall outside any process, the object that presents itself is of three kinds: kamma, the sign of kamma (kammanimitta) and the sign of destiny (gatinimitta).

M10_S02.summary: At the five doors an object is very great, great, slight or very slight; at the mind door it is clear or obscure — and the size of the object decides how far the process runs.
body: An object presents itself in six modes, four at the five sense doors and two at the mind door.
Through the five doors there are four kinds of object: very great (atimahanta), great (mahanta), slight (paritta) and very slight (atiparitta).
Through the mind door there are two: clear (vibhūta) and obscure (avibhūta).
The 'size' of the object determines how far the cognitive process will run: the greater the object, the more complete the series of stages it can support.

M10_S03.summary: With a very great object the five-door process runs its full seventeen mind-moments, from past life-continuum through to the two registration moments.
body: The full process ending in registration has exactly 17 mind-moments, set out as: B / 1-past, 2-vibrating, 3-arrest / 4-five-door adverting, 5-eye-consciousness, 6-receiving, 7-investigating, 8-determining, 9 to 15 impulsion, 16-17 registration.
B stands for the life-continuum (bhavaṅga), the mind as it flows on when no object has intruded upon it — as in deep sleep. The life-continuum is the 'resident' citta of the stream.
The first three are life-continuum moments: past life-continuum (Atītabhavaṅga), vibrating life-continuum (Bhavaṅgacalana) and arrest of the life-continuum (Bhavaṅgupaccheda).

The remaining fourteen are the 'visiting' cittas: five-door adverting (Pañcadvārāvajjana), eye-consciousness (Cakkhuviññāṇa), receiving (Sampaṭicchana), investigating (Santīraṇa), determining (Voṭṭhapana), seven moments of impulsion (Javana) and two moments of registration (Tadālambana).

This process has 7 stages and 14 visiting cittas; 46 kinds of sense-sphere citta may take part in it (the 54 sense-sphere cittas less the four pairs of sense consciousnesses not concerned); it occurs in 8 classes of person (4 worldlings and 4 attainers of fruition) and in the 11 sense-sphere planes.

The mango simile fixes all seventeen moments in the memory: lying asleep under a mango tree is the life-continuum; the mango falling is the past life-continuum; the sound disturbing one is the vibrating life-continuum; starting up and sitting is the arrest of the life-continuum.

Turning the eyes towards the sound is five-door adverting; seeing the mango is eye-consciousness; stepping over and picking it up is receiving; turning it over and inspecting it is investigating; recognising that it is ripe is determining.

Taking seven bites of the mango is the seven impulsion moments; smacking the lips twice afterwards is the two registration moments; lying down to sleep again is the return of the basic life-continuum.

M10_S04.summary: Each stage has its own task: the early stages make the object clear, impulsion fully experiences it and makes kamma, and registration enjoys what is left over.
body: Five-door adverting and the five pairs of sense consciousness, besides their own particular functions, serve to bring the object into view.
Receiving, investigating and mind-door adverting carry the further work of completing the apprehension of the object.
Impulsion (Javana) fully experiences the object: this is the stage at which the object is dealt with, and at which wholesome or unwholesome consciousness arises — the stage that makes kamma.
Registration (Tadālambana) takes up what remains of the object after impulsion has finished with it.

The impulsions in a five-door process are always sense-sphere cittas: the 12 unwholesome + 8 great wholesome sense-sphere beautiful + 8 sense-sphere functional + 1 smile-producing citta = 29 sense-sphere impulsion cittas.

M10_S06.summary: The seven impulsion moments carry the seed of kamma: the first ripens in this life, the seventh in the next, and the middle five at any time thereafter.
body: Javana comes from the root 'ju', to run swiftly. The impulsion moments carry the latent force of the deed and store the seed of kamma (Bījakamma).
The first moment is the weakest, since it arises first and has no preceding impulsion of its own kind to support it; it can give its result only in this present life — immediately effective kamma.
The seventh moment is next weakest, standing at the brink of dissolution; it gives its result only in the life immediately to come — subsequently effective kamma.

The second to the sixth moments give results at no fixed date, from the following lives onward until final Nibbāna — indefinitely effective kamma. Among them the fourth is the strongest, standing at the peak of the series as the dominant moment.
This is precisely the bridge between the cognitive process studied here and the classification of kamma by time of ripening studied in module M6.

M10_S07.summary: Registration enjoys the residue of the object after impulsion; it needs a very great or very clear object, a sense-sphere impulsion, person and object, and is performed by eleven cittas.
body: Tadā means 'that very'; ārammaṇa means object. Tadālambana therefore means 'having that same object' — also rendered as the citta that shares the object, that gleans, that picks up the remainder.

Its task is to enjoy the residue of the object left by impulsion. Two registration moments are needed because the object of the impulsions is so great: they slow the momentum down and let the stream return to its normal course.
Two things give rise to registration: a very great object in a five-door process, and a very clear object in a mind-door process.

Three conditions must hold: the impulsions must be sense-sphere impulsions; the person must be a sense-sphere being; and the object of the process must itself belong to the sense sphere. Registration never arises with a sublime or a supramundane object.

Eleven cittas perform the function of registration: the 8 great resultant sense-sphere beautiful cittas and the 3 rootless investigating cittas. Being resultants, they cannot create kamma; they merely enjoy what is left of the object.

M10_S08.summary: The mind-door process starts from within, through the life-continuum: an ordinary process of ten visiting cittas, plus ten special processes such as attaining jhāna or path.
body: The mind door is the life-continuum consciousness itself. A mind-door process is set going from within, by mind-consciousness alone, without any impact on a physical sense base.

Ordinary mind-door processes are of two kinds: the everyday process (the stream of consciousness as it runs in daily life, in four varieties according to whether the object is very clear, clear, obscure or very obscure) and the death-proximate process (occurring at the close of life, either death followed by rebirth or death followed by final Nibbāna).

The complete everyday mind-door process runs: past life-continuum – vibrating – arrest – mind-door adverting – 7 impulsions – 2 registrations – life-continuum. It has 10 visiting cittas (1 adverting + 7 impulsions + 2 registrations) and 3 stages.
Forty-one kinds of citta may occur in this process: mind-door adverting + 29 sense-sphere impulsions + 11 registration cittas. It occurs in 8 classes of person and in the 11 sense-sphere planes.

The special mind-door processes are ten: attaining jhāna, attaining the path, exercising psychic power, entering absorption, entering fruition attainment, entering the attainment of cessation, entering Nibbāna from jhāna, entering Nibbāna from psychic power, entering Nibbāna in reaction to the jhāna factors, and attaining the path at the very end of life.

M10_S09.summary: The dataset includes process-freed consciousness, but this source PDF does not treat it directly, so the topic is marked as missing from the source rather than inferred.
body: The app's dataset contains an entry for VT_VITHIMUTTA — process-freed consciousness: rebirth-linking, life-continuum and death.

On reviewing the whole of the text extracted from VDP-LoTrinhTam.pdf (62 pages), however, no separate treatment of 'Vīthimutta', consciousness outside the cognitive process, could be found. This part is therefore marked as missing from the source rather than inferred.

The one related passage found is this: for consciousness freed from the process, the object that presents itself is of three kinds — kamma, the sign of kamma and the sign of destiny (VDP-LoTrinhTam.pdf, page 2).
This gap remains to be filled from another document — possibly VDP-NguoiVaCoi.pdf — or from the complete lecture text, once the source has been verified.
